[curious, lively, starts speaking immediately] A plain steel box made your stuff cheaper. Almost everything you own rode in one, and the idea is barely seventy years old. Before the nineteen fifties, ships were loaded by hand, sack by sack and crate by crate, for days on end. Then a trucking boss named Malcom McLean had a thought. Why not lift the whole box onto the ship? In nineteen fifty-six, his ship sailed with fifty-eight of them. Loading costs fell from nearly six dollars a ton to sixteen cents. Today, the biggest ships carry them by the thousands. Look around you. Almost everything you own came in one.
